name: DuckDuckBot
follows_en: Yes, respects WWW::RobotRules (no timing note published)

ips.note: DuckDuckGo says the crawler originates from the IP addresses listed on its help page, also available as JSON at duckduckgo.com/duckduckbot.json.

vendor_quote: DuckDuckBot’s job is to constantly improve our search results and offer users the best and most secure search experience possible.

vendor_quote_source.title: DuckDuckGo Help Pages: Is DuckDuckBot related to DuckDuckGo?

what_en: DuckDuckBot is the web crawler for DuckDuckGo. DuckDuckGo says its job is to improve DuckDuckGo's search results. DuckDuckGo's help pages list DuckAssistBot on a separate page.
block_en: DuckDuckGo says DuckDuckBot respects WWW::RobotRules, so a Disallow rule addressed to DuckDuckBot in robots.txt applies to this crawler. The page says nothing about what blocking it changes in DuckDuckGo results, and nothing about DuckAssistBot.
compare_en: DuckDuckBot is the crawler for DuckDuckGo search results, while DuckAssistBot is documented by DuckDuckGo on its own help page.

sources.title: DuckDuckGo Help Pages: Is DuckDuckBot related to DuckDuckGo?

notes: The help page does not state a robots.txt token by name; it says the user agent appears as DuckDuckBot/1.1 and that it respects WWW::RobotRules, so the token DuckDuckBot is inferred from the UA product name. The JSON has 486 prefixes, all /32 (single IPv4 addresses). The 'ua' value is exactly the fragment the vendor page shows, without the Mozilla prefix. The vendor page has no robots.txt change-timing note.
answer_en: DuckDuckBot is the web crawler for DuckDuckGo, whose stated job is to improve DuckDuckGo's search results. DuckDuckGo says it respects WWW::RobotRules and publishes its IP addresses as a list in JSON form. DuckAssistBot, the fetcher for AI-assisted answers, is documented on a separate DuckDuckGo help page.
